results.name: example_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate when the target is itself one of the shown examples; observed < model means people reject examples more often than the model's near-certain membership implies (a response-level lapse).
results.code:
# name: example_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate when the target is itself one of the shown examples; observed < model means people reject examples more often than the model's near-certain membership implies (a response-level lapse).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    return rate(dist == 0)

results.name: first_minus_last_example_proximity
results.description: For sets of 2+ examples, yes rate for non-example targets within 5 of the first-shown example (and nearer it than the last) minus those within 5 of the last-shown example (nearer it than the first); observed > 0 beyond model means presentation order (first-example anchoring) matters, which the order-invariant model ignores.
results.code:
# name: first_minus_last_example_proximity
# description: For sets of 2+ examples, yes rate for non-example targets within 5 of the first-shown example (and nearer it than the last) minus those within 5 of the last-shown example (nearer it than the first); observed > 0 beyond model means presentation order (first-example anchoring) matters, which the order-invariant model ignores.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    last = ex[np.arange(len(ex)), n - 1]
    d1 = np.abs(ex[:, 0] - t)
    dl = np.abs(last - t)
    m = (n >= 2) & (dist > 0)
    return rate(m & (d1 <= 5) & (d1 < dl)) - rate(m & (dl <= 5) & (dl < d1))

results.name: shared_final_digit_distant_yes
results.description: Among sets whose examples all end in the same digit, yes rate for non-example targets with that final digit lying more than 10 from every example; observed > model means people commit to the 'ends in d' rule more firmly than the model.
results.code:
# name: shared_final_digit_distant_yes
# description: Among sets whose examples all end in the same digit, yes rate for non-example targets with that final digit lying more than 10 from every example; observed > model means people commit to the 'ends in d' rule more firmly than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    ld = ex % 10
    a = np.nanmax(ld, axis=1) == np.nanmin(ld, axis=1)
    m = a & ((ex[:, 0] % 10) == (t % 10)) & (dist > 10)
    return rate(m)

results.name: parity_skip_contrast
results.description: Among sets whose examples all share a parity, yes rate for same-parity targets 2 away from the nearest example minus opposite-parity targets 1 away; observed > model means people use parity more sharply against neighbours than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: parity_skip_contrast
# description: Among sets whose examples all share a parity, yes rate for same-parity targets 2 away from the nearest example minus opposite-parity targets 1 away; observed > model means people use parity more sharply against neighbours than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    p = np.nanmax(ex % 2, axis=1) == np.nanmin(ex % 2, axis=1)
    same = (ex[:, 0] % 2) == (t % 2)
    return rate(p & same & (dist == 2)) - rate(p & (~same) & (dist == 1))

results.name: far_unrelated_yes_floor
results.description: Yes rate for targets more than 20 from every example, outside the example range, on sets whose examples do not share a parity; observed > model means a lapse/guessing floor of yes responses the concept posterior does not predict.
results.code:
# name: far_unrelated_yes_floor
# description: Yes rate for targets more than 20 from every example, outside the example range, on sets whose examples do not share a parity; observed > model means a lapse/guessing floor of yes responses the concept posterior does not predict.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    p = np.nanmax(ex % 2, axis=1) == np.nanmin(ex % 2, axis=1)
    m = (dist > 20) & ((t < mn) | (t > mx)) & (~p)
    return rate(m)

results.name: upward_minus_downward_generalization
results.description: For targets 1-15 outside the example range, yes rate above the maximum minus yes rate below the minimum; observed > model means people extend more upward (or less downward) than the model's compressed number line predicts.
results.code:
# name: upward_minus_downward_generalization
# description: For targets 1-15 outside the example range, yes rate above the maximum minus yes rate below the minimum; observed > model means people extend more upward (or less downward) than the model's compressed number line predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    up = (t > mx) & (t - mx <= 15)
    dn = (t < mn) & (mn - t <= 15)
    return rate(up) - rate(dn)

results.name: early_minus_late_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate in a session's first 100 trials minus yes rate after trial 300; observed > model means people endorse more early and become stricter over the session, a drift the stationary model cannot produce.
results.code:
# name: early_minus_late_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate in a session's first 100 trials minus yes rate after trial 300; observed > model means people endorse more early and become stricter over the session, a drift the stationary model cannot produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).values
    return rate(ti < 100) - rate(ti >= 300)
